criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo identifies LTV exceeds 80% FFIEC supervisory limit
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the as-is LTV as 81.04% and states that it is above customary 75–80% policy limits, requiring documented credit approval of an exception. Although it does not cite FFIEC or 12 CFR Part 365 by name, it identifies the LTV exceedance over the 80% threshold and treats it as a required credit/regulatory exception item.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo recommends board exception approval for LTV exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum explicitly flags the as-is LTV of 81.04% as above customary 75–80% limits and recommends obtaining documented credit approval of any exception. In Issue J-1, it requires evidence of credit approval and any exception approved by the bank's loan committee or board of directors, and Part VII open item 14 calls for loan committee approval and exception documentation. This satisfies the criterion by recommending/noting board or committee approval and documentation for the LTV exceedance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage includes specific CREC covenant for vapor barrier
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains an express, specific covenant addressing the Bay 1 vapor barrier. Section 12.2(b) obligates Borrower to 'maintain, in good condition and working order, the vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1,' and not to penetrate, remove, damage, compromise or alter it without SCDHEC and Lender approval. Section 12.2(c) adds periodic inspection and reporting obligations; Section 7.9 restricts renovation work affecting the slab; Section 12.2(a) prohibits residential use of the Lot 7 ground floor; and Section 16.1(l) makes breach an Event of Default. The LUR is expressly identified as recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89 (Definitions of 'LUR,' Section 4.2, Exhibit B Exception 3, and Exhibit E), which also details the vapor barrier requirement. This goes far beyond a generic 'comply with environmental laws' covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage prohibits residential conversion of ground floor Lot 7/Bay 1
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains an express covenant prohibiting residential use or conversion of the ground floor of Lot 7/Bay 1, consistent with the SCDHEC land use restriction. Section 12.2(a) states Borrower shall not use, convert, lease for, permit or suffer the use of the ground floor of Lot 7 (Bay 1) for any residential purpose. This is reinforced by Section 9.3 (no residential purpose on the ground floor of Lot 7), Section 10.8 (no change of use / no residential use of Bay 1), Section 16.1(l) (breach is an Event of Default), and Exhibit E detailing the LUR restrictions. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Breach of CREC/environmental restriction is an event of default
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly ties violation of the SCDHEC land use restriction to an Event of Default. Section 16.1(l) provides that any failure to comply with the LUR or Article 12 is an Event of Default, specifically including residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7, penetration/removal/compromise of the Bay 1 vapor barrier without SCDHEC approval and Lender consent, failure to conduct required vapor barrier inspections, and modification/termination/vacation of the LUR without Lender consent. Article 12 also contains the corresponding affirmative covenants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Memo identifies CREC compliance obligation as a drafting issue
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum extensively identifies the CREC on Lot 7 arising from PCE and petroleum solvent contamination, and treats it as a drafting issue requiring specific, non-templated environmental covenants. Part IV.B-1 describes the SCDHEC land use restriction (no residential use, vapor barrier maintenance and periodic inspection), notes the title company's closer note requiring the Mortgage to contain specific LUR covenants and an Event of Default for noncompliance, and explains that Article 12 is 'purpose-built rather than templated' (§12.2(a)-(g), §16.1(l), §18.2(d), Exhibit E). Part IV.B-2 further addresses the uninspected vapor barrier and the risk of renovation work penetrating the Bay 1 slab. The risk register (item 8) and Part VII open items also flag the LUR and vapor barrier as action items. This goes well beyond a standard environmental compliance clause and satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo identifies renovation holdback gap ($900K shortfall)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the renovation funding gap in multiple places: Part III states the Holdback of $2,250,000 is $600,000 below the $2,850,000 contract sum and that 'Borrower must fund $900,000 of renovation equity'; Part V Verification Schedule item 3 confirms '$2,250,000 + $900,000' against the $3,150,000 budget; Part E-3 notes '$900,000 of equity is committed to renovation'; and the F-1 table breaks out Budget $3,150,000 / Lender Holdback $2,250,000 / Borrower equity $900,000. The $900,000 gap between the $2,250,000 holdback and the $3,150,000 renovation budget is clearly identified and discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Mortgage requires borrower equity contribution before holdback draws
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage’s renovation draw provisions address sequencing of borrower equity and lender holdback draws. Section 7.2(e) conditions each holdback disbursement on evidence that Borrower has funded, or is concurrently funding, its proportionate share of the costs covered by the draw request in accordance with Exhibit C’s funding allocation, unless Lender agrees otherwise. Exhibit C specifies a $900,000 Borrower Equity allocation by line item, and Section 7.1(c) requires Borrower to fund renovation costs in excess of the Renovation Holdback from its own funds. This satisfies the criterion by protecting Lender against funding ahead of Borrower’s equity contribution or otherwise addressing the required sequencing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo flags draw schedule shows interspersed (not equity-first) funding
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum discusses draw schedule reconciliation and retainage issues, but it does not flag that borrower equity contributions are interspersed with lender draws rather than required to be contributed first. It also does not identify the resulting risk that the holdback could be exhausted before completion due to that sequencing. The specific issue described in the criterion is therefore not mentioned.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Memo identifies Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 conflict with leasing covenants
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue C-3 in the memo expressly identifies that Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC holds a right of first refusal on Bay 2 (which the memo confirms is vacant), describing the 15-business-day match right, its survival of renewal, and its effect of adding an estimated 60–90 days to Bay 2 absorption — i.e., that the ROFR 'governs the lease-up schedule on which the whole credit story depends.' The memo ties this directly to leasing covenants: §9.6's lease-approval/Lender-consent framework, the Lowcountry exclusivity constraint on future leasing, the ROFR's interaction with the DSCR/lease-up projections (cross-referenced in F-5), and the recommendation that Lender's consent threshold be extended to all ground-floor bays because the 3,800 SF bays fall below the 5,000 SF consent trigger. It also flags the need to confirm the tenant's termination right has lapsed and to produce a Bay 2 leasing plan accounting for the ROFR. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Mortgage addresses ROFR in leasing covenant provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly addresses the Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 in its leasing covenant. Section 9.6 prohibits Borrower from entering into any new Lease that 'violates any exclusive use or right of first refusal granted to an existing tenant, including ... the right of first refusal granted to Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC with respect to Bay 2.' The ROFR is thus both acknowledged as an existing encumbrance (also noted in Exhibit D, where Bay 2 is shown as VACANT 'subject to Harmon & Wren right of first refusal,' and in the rent roll representations in Section 8.4) and made a condition of new leasing of Bay 2. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Memo identifies missing assignment consent clause in Lowcountry Provisions lease
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies in Issue C-2 that the Lowcountry Provisions lease has no assignment provision and no contractual machinery for assignment consent. It also discusses the implications for the lender’s assignment of rents, noting that the rent assignment is legally enforceable on notice under the Act but that tenant cooperation is practically important, especially in a workout, and recommends an estoppel acknowledging the assignment, a direction to pay, and a lender notice letter as fallback.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage/memo recommends estoppel certificate from Lowcountry Provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: Both documents satisfy the criterion. The Mortgage requires estoppel certificates from all tenants (including Lowcountry Provisions Inc.) as a condition to the initial advance (Section 3.5, reinforced by Section 20.1(l)) and imposes an ongoing estoppel covenant (Section 9.7). The Mortgage further specifies that the Lowcountry estoppel must acknowledge the Mortgage and the rent assignment and agree to pay Rents to Lender on notice. Separately, the issues memorandum (Issue C-2) expressly recommends obtaining an estoppel certificate from Lowcountry Provisions, noting the lease has no estoppel, assignment, or SNDA provision, and recommends a fallback of an estoppel acknowledging the assignment plus a direction to pay and a lender notice letter. Either document alone would satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage includes borrower representation re right to assign rents
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains Borrower representations and warranties regarding authority. Section 8.1 represents that Borrower has all requisite power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under the Loan Documents, and Section 8.2 represents that execution, delivery, and performance of the Loan Documents have been duly authorized and do not violate the Leases or require un obtained consents. Because Article 3 of the Mortgage effects an absolute assignment of all Leases and Rents, these representations sufficiently address Borrower’s authority to make the assignment of rents, even though there is no standalone sentence using the exact phrase “right to assign all lease rents.”

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo identifies gap between SPE requirements and operating agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the gap between the borrower's Operating Agreement and the required SPE/bankruptcy-remoteness covenants. Issue D-1, titled 'The Operating Agreement does not satisfy the Term Sheet's SPE requirements, and the amendment must be signed by all three Members,' catalogues the specific deficiencies: no independent manager or independent director (OA Summary §3.1), no separateness covenants, an overbroad purpose clause with an 'any and all activities' catch-all, no lender consent to dissolution and no bankruptcy-consent provision (OA Summary §8.1), and a 75% amendment threshold requiring at least one passive member's approval. It further states that Article 14 of the Draft Mortgage imposes the single-purpose purpose limitation, eleven separateness covenants, the Independent Manager requirement (including consent to bankruptcy, dissolution, merger and amendment of SPE provisions), and that §20.1(i) makes an executed Operating Agreement Amendment a condition precedent, with signature blocks for all three Members in Article 23. The recommendation section specifically directs circulating a form of Operating Agreement Amendment and obtaining executed originals from all three Members. Related discussions (D-2, D-3, I-2) reinforce the need for a change-of-control provision at the Member level and the omnibus member consent. The criterion is plainly satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Mortgage includes SPE covenants with independent director requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains extensive single-purpose entity covenants in Article 14, including a defined term 'Independent Manager' (Section 1.1) and Section 14.3 requiring Borrower's Operating Agreement to mandate an Independent Manager whose affirmative written consent (together with the Managing Member's) is required before any voluntary bankruptcy filing, consent to involuntary petition, admission of insolvency, assignment for creditors, dissolution, merger, or amendment of bankruptcy-remoteness provisions. Section 10.5 similarly prohibits bankruptcy filings without Independent Manager consent, and Section 14.6 acknowledges the Operating Agreement Amendment cures the prior absence of such provisions. This satisfies the requirement for an independent director/manager for bankruptcy remoteness purposes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo flags need for passive member consent to SPE restrictions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly addresses passive member consent in Part IV.D (Issue D-1): it states that because GDG holds only 72%, 'GDG cannot amend the Operating Agreement alone: at least one Passive Member must approve the amendment, and the amendment must be executed by all three Members,' and recommends requiring 'executed originals from Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC.' Risk Register item 5 and Open Items ¶21–22 likewise make the executed Operating Agreement Amendment (signed by all three Members) and an omnibus Members' consent conditions precedent. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Mortgage includes flood insurance covenant for $5M in Zone X
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.3 expressly requires Borrower to maintain flood insurance of not less than $5,000,000 and acknowledges the Property is in FEMA Flood Zone X while stating Lender requires the coverage as a Loan condition. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Memo or mortgage distinguishes contractual vs. regulatory flood insurance
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue G-1 of the drafting issues memorandum expressly distinguishes the $5,000,000 flood insurance requirement as 'a contractual requirement, not a regulatory one,' noting the Property is in FEMA Zone X, 'the federal mandatory purchase requirement does not apply,' and that the bank's flood determination should say so. The Mortgage reinforces this in Section 11.3, acknowledging Zone X with no federally mandated flood insurance while requiring coverage as an express Lender condition. Both documents make the distinction the criterion requires.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Memo identifies balcony encroachment over King Street ROW
criteria_results.reasoning: Section A-3 of the memorandum expressly addresses the balcony encroachment: it identifies the decorative iron balcony extending approximately 2.5 feet over the King Street right-of-way as a title matter (Title Commitment Exception 5 and Closer Note 2), discusses the need for an ALTA 28.1 (or equivalent) survey/encroachment endorsement rather than ALTA 9, recommends requesting an encroachment permit or license from the City of Charleston, and addresses the risk and cost of city-mandated removal (supported by the Completion Guaranty). It also records the draft treatment (§4.4 approving the encroachment as a Permitted Exception, requiring permits, and allocating removal cost to Borrower) and the recommendation to request ALTA 28.1 and a zoning endorsement. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Mortgage includes covenant to maintain encroachment permit/license
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.4 requires Borrower to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and maintain any required City of Charleston encroachment license, permit, or approval for the balcony. However, the Mortgage does not include a covenant expressly requiring Borrower not to exacerbate the balcony encroachment. Because the criterion requires both maintaining the required permit/license and not exacerbating the encroachment, the output does not fully satisfy it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula specifies which U.S. Treasury rate is used
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.8 defines the Yield Maintenance Premium by reference to the 'Treasury Rate,' and Section 5.9(b) specifically defines that term: the yield to maturity of the U.S. Treasury security having a maturity date closest to, but not exceeding, the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period, as reported in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 under 'Treasury Constant Maturities,' with linear interpolation between the two nearest published maturities where no exact match exists, and a fallback rule for publication discontinuance. Section 5.9 then prescribes the deterministic computation methodology (allocation to remaining monthly periods, interest differential, discounting at the Treasury Rate on actual/360). The formula therefore specifies precisely which Treasury rate and maturity is used, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula includes the 50 basis point spread
criteria_results.reasoning: The yield maintenance premium formula in Sections 5.8 and 5.9 expressly references the Treasury Rate plus fifty (50) basis points in calculating the interest differential, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula provides a calculable methodology
criteria_results.reasoning: Sections 5.8 and 5.9 of the mortgage provide a full computational methodology for the Yield Maintenance Premium. Section 5.8 states the premium is the greater of 1.00% of the outstanding principal or the present value of the excess of interest at the Note Rate over interest at the Treasury Rate plus 50 bps for the remaining Yield Maintenance Period. Section 5.9 then sets out step-by-step mechanics: (a) allocation of the prepaid amount to remaining monthly periods through April 15, 2029; (b) a precise definition of the discount/Treasury Rate (H.15 Treasury Constant Maturities, interpolated on an actual-day basis, determined two business days before prepayment, with a fallback source); (c) the per-period interest differential formula (prepaid amount × rate differential, floored at zero × days/360); (d) present-value discounting at the Treasury Rate on an actual/360 basis with monthly compounding; (e) a fallback if H.15 ceases publication; and (f) a requirement that Lender deliver a detailed computation. This identifies the discount rate and describes the rate-differential and present-value calculation such that a third party could compute the premium from the formula alone, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Memo identifies yield maintenance ambiguity in term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum directly addresses the yield maintenance ambiguity in Issue E-4, noting that the Term Sheet's formula is 'under-specified' — specifically the undefined 'treasury rate plus fifty (50) basis points' (whether the 50 bps attaches to the Treasury rate or the Note rate) and the Treasury Rate itself. It flags the divergence from prior markup notes and states that under South Carolina law 'the risk of unenforceability arises from ambiguity,' and that courts enforce yield maintenance provisions only where 'mathematically determinate.' It cures this in §§5.8–5.9 by defining the Treasury Rate via H.15 constant maturities with linear interpolation and a step-by-step computation, and expressly notes this is designed to eliminate the enforceability risk. The risk register (item 18) and open items list also flag this for resolution before the draft goes to borrower. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Mortgage transfer restrictions cover indirect/fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 includes express change-of-control language covering direct and indirect ownership interests in Borrower and changes of control of Controlling Members. It specifically addresses upstream changes at Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP's general partner and direct/indirect ownership changes in Graydon Development Group LLC, so it is not limited to direct borrower-level transfers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Memo identifies transfer restriction gap re fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Term Sheet's transfer-restriction carve-out for 'transfers among existing members' may permit effective control changes without Lender consent, and it specifically flags upstream changes—including transfers of interests in GDG, replacement or acquisition of Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, 'successor fund' transfers, and changes in Harborline's internal membership. This directly captures the concern that fund-level GP/LP or upstream ownership changes may fall outside the literal transfer restriction and create a control-change loophole.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: 'Existing members' exception is narrowly defined
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 1.1 explicitly defines 'Members' as 'Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC, together with any other Person that hereafter becomes a member of Borrower in accordance with Section 10.2.' The transfer restriction in Section 10.2(c)(iii) uses 'existing Members,' which ties directly to that specifically identified list of the three existing members. Moreover, the exception is further narrowed by conditions (72% cap for Graydon/Guarantor, 51% floor for Graydon, Graydon must remain Managing Member, and no change of control), preventing unintended loopholes. Thus the exception is narrow and specifically identifies the three existing members, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Memo identifies tight timeline between completion and DSCR testing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the timing mismatch: substantial completion is June 15, 2026 (14 months after closing), while DSCR testing begins with the quarter ending June 30, 2027 (month 24/first test). In Issue E-8 it discusses the intervening period, notes there is no DSCR covenant or debt service support during that window, and flags the 'AGGRESSIVE TIMELINE' for Suite B lease-up before the first test. Issue E-1 separately concludes that current/projected in-place income is insufficient to satisfy the 1.25x DSCR covenant at any occupancy. Thus the criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Mortgage includes DSCR cure mechanism or cash sweep provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.5 ('DSCR Shortfall; Cure') expressly provides an equity cure/reserve deposit mechanism: if DSCR falls below 1.25:1.00 on any DSCR Test Date, Borrower may within 30 days deposit with Lender, as additional Collateral, an amount equal to the shortfall (1.25 × Annual Debt Service minus Net Operating Income for the period). Amounts are held as additional Collateral, released upon achieving 1.25:1.00 over two consecutive test dates, and the provision caps such deposits at two over the loan term. The DSCR covenant (Section 13.1, first test June 30, 2027) is thus not a bare hard default—it is paired with a protective cure/deposit mechanism, exactly the kind of provision the criterion contemplates. The event of default in Section 16.1(g) only triggers if DSCR < 1.25:1.00 on two consecutive test dates without cure under Section 13.5, confirming the cure mechanism is integrated. PASS.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Memo identifies chain of title concern for vacated Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: Section A-1 of the memorandum expressly identifies that title to the vacated Anson Lane strip derives from a quitclaim deed from the City of Charleston recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, quotes the title company's statement that 'no warranties of title were provided,' explains the chain of title concern (coverage quality/insurability for Parcel Two), and recommends obtaining written confirmation from Prestige Title that the Policy will insure fee simple title to the parcel and that an ALTA 34 endorsement (or equivalent) will be issued. It also flags revisiting the collateral description if coverage cannot be obtained. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Mortgage legal description includes Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit A of the Mortgage contains a dedicated 'PARCEL TWO (vacated Anson Lane strip)' description expressly identifying the strip formerly known as Anson Lane, vacated and closed by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084, and conveyed by Quitclaim Deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443 in the RMC Office. The Anson Lane strip is also incorporated in the defined term 'Land' in Section 1.1 and in the granting clause at Section 2.1(a), and is addressed separately in Section 4.5. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage explicitly identifies the lender as Calverley Heritage Bank in the title, preamble, and notice provisions.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies lender entity type and address
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage identifies the lender as Calverley Heritage Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank insured by the FDIC, with its principal office at 412 Whitaker Street, Savannah, Georgia 31401.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies borrower name as Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies borrower entity type and address
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage identifies the borrower as Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC, a South Carolina limited liability company, with its principal office at 88 Broad Street, Suite 200, Charleston, South Carolina 29401. Both the entity type and address match the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct loan amount of $14,750,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage states the principal amount as $14,750,000.00 in the header and repeatedly identifies the loan amount as $14,750,000.00 in the recitals and related provisions.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct maturity date of April 15, 2030
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines the Maturity Date as April 15, 2030, which is five years from the stated Closing Date of April 15, 2025.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states interest rate as Daily SOFR + 285 bps
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the Applicable Spread as 2.85% (285 basis points) and states the interest rate is Daily SOFR plus the Applicable Spread, subject to the SOFR Floor. The benchmark and spread are correct and present.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states SOFR floor of 3.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines "SOFR Floor" as three percent (3.00%) per annum and uses it in the Interest Rate calculation, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct default rate: applicable rate + 5.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 1.1 defines the Default Rate as the Interest Rate otherwise applicable plus five percent (5.00%) per annum, and Section 5.3 applies that Default Rate upon an Event of Default. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month interest-only period from closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the Interest-Only Period as commencing on the Closing Date (April 15, 2025) and ending April 15, 2027 — exactly 24 months. Section 5.1 confirms that each monthly installment during the Interest-Only Period consists solely of accrued interest, with principal amortization beginning May 15, 2027.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 25-year amortization schedule after IO period
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly provides that, after the Interest-Only Period, monthly installments will fully amortize the then-outstanding principal over a twenty-five (25) year amortization schedule, and the Annual Debt Service definition likewise references a 25-year amortization period.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month lockout period with no prepayment
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines the Lockout Period as commencing on the Closing Date (April 15, 2025) and ending on April 15, 2027, which is exactly 24 months. Section 5.7 expressly prohibits any prepayment during the Lockout Period. Therefore, the 24-month no-prepayment lockout requirement is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes yield maintenance premium prepayment from month 25 through month 48
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage defines a Yield Maintenance Period from April 16, 2027 through April 15, 2029, which corresponds to months 25 through 48 of the loan term. Section 5.8 requires payment of a Yield Maintenance Premium for prepayments during that period, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes open prepayment with no premium during final 12 months
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.10 expressly permits open prepayment, in whole or in part, during the final twelve months of the Loan term (April 16, 2029 through the Maturity Date, i.e., months 49–60), without any prepayment premium, penalty, yield maintenance amount, or other charge.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes late charge of 5% with 10-day grace period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.4 provides for a late charge equal to 5% of any overdue monthly installment of principal and/or interest not received within 10 calendar days after the due date, which satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes DSCR covenant of at least 1.25x tested quarterly
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 13.1 requires Borrower to maintain a DSCR of not less than 1.25 to 1.00, and Section 1.1 defines DSCR Test Date as the last day of each calendar quarter, so the covenant is tested quarterly at the required minimum.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage DSCR testing commences 24 months after closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The Mortgage defines DSCR Test Date as the last day of each calendar quarter beginning with the calendar quarter ending June 30, 2027, and Section 13.1(a) states DSCR testing commences with that date. Given the Closing Date of April 15, 2025, this is the quarter-end following the 24-month anniversary (April 15, 2027), satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes tax and insurance escrow provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.1(a) of the Mortgage expressly requires Borrower to deposit with Lender, on the Closing Date and on each Payment Date thereafter, an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual amounts, as estimated by Lender, required to pay all real property taxes and assessments affecting the three tax parcels, and all premiums for the property, flood, liability and other insurance required under Article 11 (together with anticipated deductibles). Section 6.1(b) confirms these amounts are held in the Tax and Insurance Escrow Account and applied toward taxes and insurance premiums when due. The criterion is therefore satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes capital replacement reserve of $0.25/SF/year
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.2 of the Mortgage expressly establishes a Capital Replacement Reserve requiring monthly deposits of $645.83, derived from $0.25/SF/year × 31,000 SF = $7,750/year ÷ 12 months. The math is correct ($7,750/12 = $645.83), and the provision includes disbursement mechanics and Lender's right to reassess the deposit amount. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes TI/LC reserve with $150,000 initial deposit
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.3 establishes a Tenant Improvement and Leasing Commission Reserve Account, requires an initial $150,000 deposit at closing, and requires replenishment to the full $150,000 from Borrower's own funds upon any drawdown. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes renovation reserve/holdback of $2,250,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The Mortgage defines the Renovation Holdback as $2,250,000 (Section 1.1) and establishes a Renovation Holdback Account (Section 6.4) funded from loan proceeds, consistent with $14,750,000 minus a $12,500,000 initial advance. Article 7 and Section 20.2 specify draw-basis disbursement subject to conditions: AIA G702/G703 architect-certified applications (Section 7.2(a)), conditional and unconditional lien waivers (Section 7.2(b)), title date-down endorsements (Section 7.2(c)), inspection, borrower proportionate funding, and no default. Retainage (10%, $225,000) and the $900,000 borrower equity share are correctly computed and consistent. The amount and draw conditions match the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes initial advance of $12,500,000 at closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage repeatedly states the loan principal is $14,750,000 and separately identifies a $2,250,000 Renovation Holdback and $6,200,000 equity contribution. However, the figure $12,500,000 never appears anywhere in the document, and no provision states, describes, or quantifies an 'initial advance at closing' of $12,500,000. Section 20.1 (Conditions to the Initial Advance) lists conditions but no advance amount. While $12,500,000 is mathematically derivable ($14,750,000 − $2,250,000), the criterion requires the mortgage to state or reflect the initial advance amount, and the document does not do so explicitly or in any identified advance provision. The initial advance amount is therefore not mentioned.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage legal description includes Lots 7, 8, and 9 of Hampstead Village Plat
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage’s legal description expressly includes Lots 7, 8, and 9 of the Hampstead Village Plat, recorded in Plat Book 41 at Page 218, and identifies all three corresponding Tax Map parcels.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage legal description includes all three tax parcel numbers
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's legal description and related property definitions expressly reference all three tax parcel numbers: Tax Map Nos. 460-12-04-007, 460-12-04-008, and 460-12-04-009. Exhibit A separately lists each parcel with the corresponding number.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes absolute assignment of rents (not collateral assignment)
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains Article 3, titled 'ABSOLUTE ASSIGNMENT OF LEASES AND RENTS.' Section 3.1 expressly states that Borrower 'unconditionally, absolutely and presently grants, transfers and assigns' all Leases and Rents, that the assignment is 'without reservation of any kind,' and that it 'is an absolute and present assignment and not a collateral assignment given as additional security only.' It further invokes the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act (S.C. Code Ann. § 29-3-100 et seq.), states perfection occurs upon recording, and clarifies the assignment is in addition to the mortgage lien. The license-back to collect rents prior to default (Section 3.2) is a standard feature of an absolute assignment and does not render it collateral. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage grants security interest in personal property and UCC collateral
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly grants a security interest in personal property and UCC collateral, including equipment, fixtures, accounts, deposit accounts, general intangibles, and proceeds (Sections 2.1(d)-(l) and 2.2). It also expressly references UCC-1 financing statements and fixture filings, including filings with the South Carolina Secretary of State (Sections 2.2, 2.4, 19.3, and 20.1(a)).

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes security interest in insurance and condemnation proceeds
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes both insurance proceeds and condemnation awards within the collateral. Section 2.1(f) grants a lien/security interest in 'all insurance proceeds, condemnation awards, payments in lieu thereof and other payments' arising from damage, destruction, taking, or diminution in value of the Property. Article 15 also assigns insurance proceeds and condemnation awards to Lender. Thus both categories are included.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes security interest in permits, licenses, and development rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 2.1(g) expressly includes permits, licenses, entitlements, development rights, subdivision rights, air rights, governmental authorizations, zoning rights, and vested rights relating to the Property within the collateral, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes security interest in contracts and project documents
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes contracts and project documents as collateral. Section 2.1(h) grants a security interest in all construction and architectural agreements, warranties, guaranties, indemnities, and claims relating to construction or renovation, expressly including Borrower's interest in the Construction Contract and Contractor warranties/guaranties. Section 2.1(j) covers plans, specifications, drawings, surveys, studies, reports, and books and records. The Construction Contract is defined as the agreement with Beaufort Builders Group LLC, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes covenant against subordinate financing without consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.1 expressly prohibits Borrower, without Lender's prior written consent, from incurring, creating, assuming, permitting or suffering any lien, mortgage, security interest, pledge, encumbrance, subordinate or mezzanine debt, preferred equity, or other financing arrangement secured by the Property or any interest in Borrower. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes transfer restriction with 10% individual / 25% aggregate thresholds
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 (Transfer Restrictions) of the mortgage expressly prohibits transfers of direct or indirect ownership interests in Borrower without Lender's prior written consent, subject only to enumerated Permitted Transfers. Clause (c) of the Permitted Transfers permits 'a transfer of direct membership interests in Borrower that does not exceed ten percent (10%) individually or twenty-five percent (25%) in the aggregate (measured cumulatively from the Closing Date) and that does not result in any Person or group of Persons acquiring control of Borrower.' Because the general prohibition in Section 10.2(b) applies to all ownership transfers and only the sub-10%/25% transfers are carved out as permitted without consent, transfers exceeding those specific thresholds require Lender's prior written consent. The carve-outs are also further qualified (no control acquisition, affiliated transferee for passive investors holding <20%, no increase in Guarantor's 72% stake or decrease below 51%). Although the lettering/numbering in Section 10.2 is internally inconsistent (clause (c) followed by (ii)-(iv), then (e)-(f) with no (d)), the substantive 10% individual / 25% aggregate thresholds are clearly present and operative, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: SPE covenant: borrower restricted to owning/operating the Property only
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes an express SPE covenant in Article 14, Section 14.1, stating that Borrower shall not engage in any business or activity other than the ownership, operation, renovation, leasing, management and disposition of the Property and incidental activities, and that its sole purpose is limited to such activities. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: SPE covenant: no voluntary bankruptcy without independent director consent
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes an express SPE covenant requiring independent manager consent before any voluntary bankruptcy filing. Section 10.5 prohibits voluntary bankruptcy without prior approval of the Independent Manager and Lender, and Section 14.3(a) further requires the Independent Manager's affirmative written consent before Borrower may file a voluntary petition. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: SPE covenant: separate books and no commingling
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes SPE covenants in Article 14.2 requiring Borrower to maintain its own separate books of account and financial records, and expressly prohibiting Borrower from commingling its funds or assets with those of any Member, Affiliate, manager, or other Person. Both required provisions are present.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes property insurance covenant (all-risk, replacement cost)
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 11, Section 11.1 expressly requires Borrower to maintain comprehensive all-risk (special form) property insurance covering the Property and Improvements on a replacement cost basis, with agreed amount/waiver of coinsurance. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes CGL insurance requirement ($2M occ. / $5M agg.)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 (Commercial General Liability) expressly requires Borrower to maintain CGL insurance "with minimum limits of Two Million and No/100 Dollars ($2,000,000.00) per occurrence and Five Million and No/100 Dollars ($5,000,000.00) in the aggregate, naming Lender as an additional insured," and further specifies coverage for premises liability, operations, products/completed operations, personal and advertising injury, and contractual liability. This meets the $2M/$5M threshold in the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage requires annual audited financial statements within 120 days of FYE
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.3(a) of the mortgage requires Borrower to deliver annual audited financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP by an independent CPA firm within 120 days after the end of each fiscal year. This matches the criterion exactly.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage requires quarterly rent rolls within 30 days of quarter-end
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 13.3(c) expressly requires Borrower to deliver quarterly rent rolls for the Property within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes borrower net worth covenant of $1,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 expressly requires Borrower to maintain at all times a net worth of not less than $1,000,000, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes borrower liquidity covenant of $500,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes a borrower liquidity covenant in Section 13.2, requiring liquid assets of not less than $500,000.00, defined as cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities, and unencumbered deposits at federally insured institutions.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes events of default section covering payment default, covenant default, and bankruptcy/insolvency
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 16 of the Mortgage contains an Events of Default section. Section 16.1(a) covers Payment default (failure to make payment when due), Section 16.1(b) covers Covenant Default (breach of any covenant or obligation in the Mortgage or other Loan Document), and Section 16.1(d) covers Bankruptcy/Insolvency (voluntary petition, receiver consent, assignment for benefit of creditors, inability to pay debts, involuntary petition not dismissed, etc.). All three required categories are expressly included, so the criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes remedies section (acceleration, foreclosure, receiver)
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage has a remedies article with judicial foreclosure consistent with South Carolina law, appointment of a receiver, UCC remedies, rent collection, and entry. However, it does not expressly provide for acceleration of the debt within the remedies section or as a general remedy upon default; acceleration is only referenced in a specific transfer-restriction provision (Section 10.2(e)). Because the criterion requires the remedies section to provide for acceleration, the output is deficient.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage references the guaranty by Neil Ashford Graydon
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage repeatedly references Neil Ashford Graydon as Guarantor. Recital D expressly identifies 'Neil Ashford Graydon, an individual residing at 14 Church Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29401 ("Guarantor")' and states he has agreed to execute the Guaranty, Completion Guaranty, Payment Guaranty and Environmental Indemnity. The Guaranty is also defined as a Loan Document (Article 1.1), referenced in Article 19.1, Article 18.3, Article 23.2, and the signature blocks include the Guarantor's Acknowledgment. The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes granting clause with mortgage lien language
criteria_results.reasoning: The document contains multiple explicit granting clauses using the operative words 'grant,' 'mortgage,' 'convey,' and 'assign' to convey a lien interest in the Property to Lender as security for the loan. The preamble granting clause states Borrower 'hereby grants, bargains, sells, aliens, remises, releases, conveys, mortgages, assigns, transfers and sets over to Lender, and grants to Lender a lien upon and security interest in' the Property, and Section 2.1 ('Grant of Mortgage Lien') repeats the operative language and expressly grants a 'first-priority lien upon and security interest in' the Land, Improvements, and related collateral to secure the Obligations. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage property address is 520-534 King Street, Charleston, SC 29403
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage explicitly identifies the property address as 520–534 King Street, Charleston, South Carolina 29403 in the header and repeatedly throughout the document (including the Land definition, Exhibit A, and various sections). The address matches the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes tax payment/escrow covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes a tax payment/escrow covenant. Section 6.1 establishes a Tax and Insurance Escrow Account requiring monthly deposits equal to 1/12 of estimated annual real property taxes and insurance premiums, with Lender applying funds to taxes as they become due and an obligation to cover any deficiency. Additionally, Section 9.4 (Taxes and Assessments) requires the borrower to pay and discharge all real property taxes and assessments before delinquency, deliver tax bills, and notify Lender of tax reassessments. These provisions satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes compliance with laws covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes a compliance with laws covenant in Section 9.3, requiring Borrower to comply at all times with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, orders, ordinances, and governmental requirements applicable to the Property and Borrower's business.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes maintenance/repair covenant for the Property
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains an express maintenance/repair covenant in Section 9.2 ('Maintenance and Repairs'), requiring Borrower to keep the Property, including all Improvements, fixtures, building systems, common areas, landscaping, parking areas, and the vacated Anson Lane strip, in good order, condition, and repair consistent with comparable mixed-use properties, to promptly make all repairs, renewals, replacements, and restorations necessary to preserve value and utility, and prohibiting waste. Related covenants (e.g., Sections 9.1, 9.3, 9.5, 9.15, and Article 15 restoration obligations) reinforce the requirement. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage references South Carolina as governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 22.1 expressly states that the Mortgage is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of South Carolina, without regard to conflicts of law principles.

criteria_results.title: Issues memo is produced as a separate deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent's output is a standalone 'Drafting Issues Memorandum' — a distinct deliverable from the mortgage instrument itself, addressed to the client, with a risk register, issue analysis (collateral/title, environmental, leases, SPE, loan economics, renovation, insurance, covenants, transfer restrictions, regulatory/closing), open items, source-conflict reconciliation, and verification schedules. It thoroughly identifies legal, commercial, and drafting issues. This satisfies the criterion of producing a separate issues memorandum distinct from the mortgage document.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage document is produced as a deliverable
criteria_results.reasoning: The agent's output is a complete Mortgage and Security Agreement document, including preamble, recitals, granting clauses, articles on definitions, collateral, assignment of leases and rents, covenants, events of default, remedies, non-recourse carve-outs, exhibits (legal description, permitted exceptions, renovation budget, rent roll, LUR), signature blocks, and notarial acknowledgment. It clearly satisfies the criterion of producing a mortgage and security agreement deliverable.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance enforceability under SC law discussed
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum addresses yield maintenance enforceability under South Carolina law in Issue E-4. It states that 'South Carolina courts have enforced yield maintenance provisions that are mathematically determinate; the risk of unenforceability arises from ambiguity, and the drafted formula is designed to eliminate it.' This discusses SC-law enforceability and the risk that an imprecise formula could be held unenforceable, and the memo connects the drafting of a determinate formula to avoiding that risk. It also flags in Part IX that no opinion is rendered on enforceability, and E-7 discusses penalty characterization for the related default rate/late charge. The core requirement—discussion of SC-law enforceability of the yield maintenance premium and the ambiguity/enforceability risk—is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: SC Assignment of Rents Act referenced for rent assignment
criteria_results.reasoning: The Draft Mortgage expressly references the South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act with a citation in Article 3, Section 3.1: "this Article 3 constitute an absolute assignment of Rents within the meaning of the Uniform Assignment of Rents Act as enacted in the State of South Carolina (S.C. Code Ann. § 29-3-100 et seq.)", and ties perfection of the rent assignment to recording under that framework. The issues memorandum (Part IV, C-1) also discusses the Act and the same citation in connection with the assignment of rents provisions. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage references SCDHEC NFA letter and land use restriction recording info
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage extensively references both the SCDHEC No Further Action determination dated August 12, 2021 (Site ID SC-29403-0772) and the land use restriction recorded in Deed Book 1203 at Page 89, Charleston County RMC. These appear in the definition of 'LUR' (Section 1.1), Article 12.2, Exhibit B (Permitted Exceptions, item 3), and Exhibit E (dedicated to the Land Use Restriction and Institutional Controls, citing the recorded instrument, SCDHEC Site ID, and the August 12, 2021 NFA letter). The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes renovation draw conditions (architect cert, lien waivers, title endorsement)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.2 requires each renovation draw to include an architect-certified AIA G702/G703 application, conditional and unconditional lien waivers from the contractor and applicable subcontractors, and a title date-down endorsement confirming no intervening liens. All three specified conditions are present.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes security interest in reserve/escrow accounts
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes reserve and escrow accounts in the collateral. Section 2.1(e) grants a lien and security interest in all deposits, accounts, reserves, and escrows established in connection with the Loan, including the Reserve Accounts and all sums therein. Section 6.5(a) separately grants Lender a security interest in each Reserve Account and states each is part of the Collateral, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage recitals reference the promissory note
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's Recital B expressly references a Promissory Note of even date in the original principal amount of $14,750,000, identifying it as the 'Note' evidencing the Loan. The document also repeatedly refers to the Note in defined terms and operative provisions.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes environmental indemnity or reference to separate environmental indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains extensive environmental provisions and expressly references a separate Environmental Indemnity Agreement as a required Loan Document, including definitions, recitals, Article 12.4, Article 19.2, and conditions precedent. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage addresses condemnation/eminent domain proceedings
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains extensive condemnation/eminent domain provisions. Article 15 — Casualty and Condemnation includes Section 15.1 (borrower must give prompt notice of any actual or threatened condemnation or exercise of eminent domain), Section 15.2 (restoration obligations following a taking), Section 15.3 (application of condemnation awards, with Lender's right to elect restoration or application to the Obligations, and thresholds/conditions), and Section 15.3(d) (irrevocable assignment to Lender of all condemnation awards, with Lender appointed attorney-in-fact to collect, settle and apply them). The granting clause in Section 2.1(f) also assigns condemnation awards and payments in lieu thereof as collateral, and Section 2.1(l) captures proceeds. This fully satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes casualty/damage provisions and insurance proceeds application
criteria_results.reasoning: The output contains a dedicated Article 15 ('Casualty and Condemnation') that expressly provides for notice of casualty (15.1), restoration obligations (15.2), and lender's control over the application of insurance proceeds—including the right to hold proceeds in escrow, elect between restoration and payment of the Obligations, apply proceeds without prepayment premium, and an irrevocable assignment of proceeds with power of attorney (15.3(a)-(d))—plus Section 15.4 on lender's right to apply proceeds notwithstanding objections. Article 11 (e.g., Sections 11.1, 11.4, 11.7) further addresses insurance coverage and application of proceeds, confirming the required casualty/damage and proceeds-application provisions are present.
